title: Control: a record of scalars survives reconstruct() as a writable datum
rationale: The good-input drill for the DATUM mode, and the reason the mode is not a control that appears present and does nothing. Without it, a DATUM implementation that hardcoded validatesAgainstSchema=false and binaryEncodes=false would make every DATUM DEFECT row pass and nobody would ever know. It is also the row that turns RED the day reconstruct() is repaired in a way that breaks the simple case.
catchesBugClass: Proves the DATUM mode's three new gates can return true, so a false from any DEFECT row is signal rather than a constant. Also catches a regression where reconstruct() starts failing on the trivial case - a builder change that stops setting explicitly-null nullable fields, for instance, which would make build() throw or drop the key.
cannotCatch: It is entirely flat, which is exactly the condition under which the code works, so it cannot catch anything the nested-record rows are about. It exercises no logical type, no enum, no fixed and no bytes; avro-logical-type-datum-is-writable-control covers those separately.

predicted.detail: Every field is a scalar, so mapToGenericRecord's one-level copy is sufficient: validate passes, no non-record path is reported, the datum encodes, and avroDoc equals avroBaseline.
